summary: In a usual survival guide the map is the crucial thing because, through our map we are going and where we are now. And in a interplanetary mission in  mars would have survival guide too! So,  we build a map for mars with there coordinates and names , and through map you can know the average temperature , pressure , and altitude .
details:
Features and details of our project ☄️🌌

1. Map 🗺️

Mars shaded (celestia) : This map shows exact surface of mars. It is a 16384 x 8192 pix map with 5x zoom capability

And this picture is taken by NASA Viking Orbiters 1 & 2 using VIS cameras, and VIS camera can capture the Visible spectrum light or in simple words the camera which can capture normal photo

Open plantary Map : This map visualize the surface of the mars . OpenPlanetaryMap is developed by the OpenPlanetary community And it is an open-source, and we use it in our project to show the big picture 🖼️

MOLA Color Elevation : Mola sand for Mars Orbiter Laser
Altimeter means it uses LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging)—specifically Time-of-Flight (ToF) Laser Altimetry
And uses
d=c*t/2
Equation to measure the altitude c is the speed of light but it is actually the velocity of wave and t is the time taken and divided into 2 for only one way because the wave travel from emitter to ground, then ground to receiver, so that we divided into two.
It's 46,080 × 23,040 px picture with 5x,And taken in NASA Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) via the MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter) instrument 600+ million laser shots in 1999–2001
And it serves the altitude in colour formate like red for High altitude and blue is low altitude.

Mars Hill shade : In this map light and shadow effects to represent the surface structure of Mars And there is 46,080 × 23,040 pixel with 6x zoom, and it's a mixture of MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter),HRSC (High Resolution Stereo Camera).

2. Locations 📍

The dots represents the land marks in mars. And it is divided into two colors

Green 🟢

:--This is well studied ,most of the rovers prefer this site as landing sites of planetary mission and we prefer that places as the future space-base

Orange🟠

:-- This is not well studied,and we don't have that much idea of that..

3. Distance 📏

We use HAVERSINE Formula 🧪↓↓↓↓↓↓

Δφ = φ2 − φ1 and Δλ = λ2 − λ1

a = sin²(Δφ / 2) + cos(φ1) × cos(φ2) × sin²(Δλ / 2)

c = 2 × sin-1 (√a)

d = R × c

•φ1, φ2 = latitude of point 1 and point 2, in radians
•λ1, λ2 = longitude of point 1 and point 2, in radians
•R = radius of the sphere is 3,501.99 km, I know that the radius of mars is approximately 3,389.5 km it's for space-craft with altitude 110km
•Converting degrees to radians: radians = degrees × π / 180
